governance.attested_by: miso22 offer-curve 2026-06-28 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso21-cc-border-anchor)
governance.note: One STRUCTURAL/ARCHITECTURAL lever on top of miso21 (all of which are retained byte-for-byte: export cap, cc_intermediate_split, miso_pjm_border_anchor): give MISO its own ISO-specific gas offer curve (_MISO_OFFER_CURVE in scripts/run_calibration.py), the same offer-curve-override design PJM (_PJM_OFFER_CURVE), NYISO (_NYISO_OFFER_CURVE) and CAISO already use, deep-merged via _deep_merge_offer_curve gated strictly on iso=="MISO". BEFORE this lever MISO was the only large multi-zone ISO with no branch: it fell through EVERY offer_curve_by_group ternary to the generic non-PJM/non-ERCOT/non-NEISO `else`, whose band multipliers were fit to ERCOT plants (Colorado Bend II / Wolf Hollow II) and never validated for MISO -- including the 13.15x ERCOT-CT ORDC `peak` wall that PJM and CAISO already discarded. Two named gas classes change, every other class/band keeps the generic default (coal / CC_CHP / CT_CHP / ST_GAS unchanged): (1) CC_REGULAR econ ramp flattened econ_low 1.06->0.95 / econ_high 1.27->1.08 to MISO's MEASURED all-baseload CC heat-rate shape (bin_assignments_MISO.csv: 44 CC_REGULAR plants, cap-weighted HR 7.44; thermal_tranches_MISO.csv: median CF 50-150%, mean ~90% -- the incremental energy of an already-committed baseload CC is ~flat at ~0.93x its own average HR, NOT a rising start-cost-amortized ERCOT duct-fire ramp), KEEPING the cheap min-stable-load committed base (0.92) and the physically-real F-class duct-burner scarcity peak (2.25) and the per-plant peaking band (cc_peaking_per_plant) -- only the operating-range ramp is corrected, never the duct-fire peak (rule #11). This is the SAME flat curve miso21 validated via the cc_intermediate_split CC_INTERMEDIATE cohort routing; promoting it to the CC_REGULAR BASE makes MISO's CC correct even on a non-split run and renders CC_INTERMEDIATE == CC_REGULAR for MISO's all-baseload fleet (the split is now a near-no-op for MISO, retained for genuinely MIXED CC duty -- a future MISO peaker CC, or another ISO). (2) CT_PEAKER peak capped 13.15->4.00: MISO's energy offer cap is ~$1000-2000/MWh (the ELMP shadow price plus the Reserve Demand Curve / RDT scarcity adder), NOT ERCOT's $5000 ORDC, so a 13x heat-rate wall is far too high and inflates the high-price tail -- the same reasoning PJM used to cap its CT_PEAKER at 4.0; committed (1.55) and econ ramp (1.27->1.98) are left at the generic shape (only the $5000-ORDC peak is the ERCOT artifact). MISO currently shows 0 scarcity (>$200) hours, so this is FORWARD-CORRECTNESS (removing an inherited tail that would mis-fire in a forecast), not a live price change. Both bands trace to measured CAMPD heat rates and MISO market design (offer cap), assign an offer SHAPE, never pin measured output, and are not tuned to a price/volume residual (rules #1/#11). This lever is judged a keeper because it is the MOST STRUCTURALLY FAITHFUL MISO config (ISO-specific curve replacing an ERCOT-fit inheritance + correct measured CC base + MISO-cap-consistent CT peak), NOT because it lowers MAE -- per rule #1 a structurally-correct mechanism stays in even when the residual barely moves.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible end-to-end. Config-build verification: _calibration_config(year, 'MISO', ...).offer_curve_by_group resolves CC_REGULAR={committed 0.92, econ_low 0.95, econ_high 1.08, peak 2.25} and CT_PEAKER={committed 1.55, econ_low 1.27, econ_high 1.98, peak 4.0}; CC_INTERMEDIATE == CC_REGULAR for MISO; ERCOT/PJM/NYISO/CAISO/SPP/NEISO offer_curve_by_group dicts are BYTE-IDENTICAL to pre-lever (diffed all seven ISOs). The new curve is recorded verbatim in the bundle run_config.json. Solved 2023/2024/2025 in one --year invocation to results/calibration/MISO/miso22_offer_curve (solo; per-year RSS released between years, sequential; P2 commitment off, MISO default). Per-fuel vs EIA-923 (model / 923): 2023 gas 226.6/249.0 coal 164.4/184.0; 2024 gas 238.6/257.8 coal 162.7/175.1; 2025 gas 216.2/207.6 coal 214.8/201.0. Net interchange (EIA +=export, model / actual): 2023 -38.6/-37.9, 2024 -16.7/-23.1, 2025 -5.6/-19.0; interchange duration RMSE 819 / 1054 / 1728 MW. Prices: avg 31.5 / 28.9 / 38.4, max 58.4 / 70.3 / 70.8, 0 scarcity (>$200) hours, 0 negative-price hours -- the CT-wall cap introduced NO new scarcity/negative artifact. METRIC-NEUTRAL vs keeper miso21 (this run already ran --cc-intermediate-split, which had already routed MISO's baseload CC cohort to the flat CC_INTERMEDIATE curve, so promoting the BASE to flat is a near-no-op for THIS run; the CT-wall cap has zero dispatch effect at 0 scarcity hours): every C1 class is within +-0.6 TWh of miso21 (2023 CC_REGULAR +25.6 vs +25.1, CT_PEAKER -19.6 vs -19.6, ST_GAS -7.4 vs -7.3) and C2 2025 system volume is marginally better (gas -11.4% vs -11.5%, coal +11.8% vs +12.0%). The value is architectural consolidation + a correct CC base + the removed ERCOT wall, with interchange/EB/prices no worse.
governance.git_note: _MISO_OFFER_CURVE added in scripts/run_calibration.py with a MISO merge block (deep-merge gated on iso=="MISO") right after the NYISO block. No new flag: the curve applies automatically on iso=="MISO", mirroring how PJM/NYISO are effectively ISO-default (no ScenarioConfig field added). With iso!="MISO" the build is byte-identical for every other ISO and year (forecast included). All miso21 levers unchanged: --miso-seam-export-limit, --cc-intermediate-split (ScenarioConfig.cc_intermediate_split, now a no-op for MISO's all-baseload fleet but retained for mixed duty), --miso-pjm-border-anchor, and the firm-import / seam-flow / coal-mustrun / sigmoid stack. The off-by-default opposite-thesis probe _MISO_CC_COAL_REBALANCE (--miso-cc-coal-rebalance) is untouched and still deep-merges on top when set.

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS to fix in a later lever, NOT an accepted measured-input limitation, so the determination is honestly NOT-YET (a structural/architectural consolidation, not a residual-closing pass). miso22 is metric-neutral vs miso21, so the SAME misses remain, localized to: (1) MERIT-ORDER SUBSTITUTION / RESIDUAL GAS-CC OVER-vs-UNDER: at the CLASS level the model over-runs cheap CC_REGULAR (2023 +25.6, 2024 +25.4 TWh vs EIA-923) and under-runs the peakier CT_PEAKER (-19.6 / -15.3) and ST_GAS (-7.4 / -9.6), while the gas FAMILY nets to an under-run (gas 226.6 vs 249.0 and 238.6 vs 257.8, -22 / -19 TWh). The flat CC base is the structurally-correct MISO CC offer (measured ~0.93x-avg incremental); the +25 CC over-run is therefore NOT a CC-offer error to fix by un-flattening the curve (that would be an unphysical fit to volume, rule #11) but the symptom of the IMPORT UNDER-RUN below -- the model cannot import enough, so cheap domestic CC fills the gap and cannibalizes CT/ST/coal. (2) 2025 DEAR-GAS COAL OVER-RUN: coal 214.8 vs 201.0 EIA-923 (+13.8 TWh) -- the dominant 2025 miss (coal take-or-pay / PRB passthrough offer level in dear gas), unaddressed by this offer-curve lever. (3) IMPORT UNDER-RUN 2024/2025: net interchange -16.7 vs -23.1 and -5.6 vs -19.0 -- MISO still under-imports by ~6 / ~13 TWh; a MISO-LMP-LEVEL item (MISO's own dual sits too close to the re-anchored PJM border to pull the full measured eastern transfer), the root cause of (1). (4) PRICE TAIL / SCARCITY (C3c): 0 model scarcity hours vs 30/37/88 actual -- MISO's ELMP/RDT scarcity-pricing mechanism (reserve demand curve adder) is not yet modeled; capping the CT peak at 4.0 is forward-correct but does not by itself create the tail (the missing piece is the reserve-demand co-optimization, a separate lever). (5) ENERGY-BALANCE metric (-13.4 / -7.4 / -0.1) and 2025 STORAGE THROUGHPUT (+1253%) carry over from miso21 unchanged (the EB 2024 figure is partly an EIA-930 MISO Demand/Net-gen/Interchange data-imbalance artifact, not a model demand error). None of these is closable by an adder/haircut/pin/rescale to a residual (rule #12); each is a separate measured-grounded lever (MISO ELMP/RDT scarcity co-optimization; coal dear-gas offer; MISO LMP level / SPP-South seam pricing).
